text.text: I'll start by reading the card to understand the contract

I have the card. The contract: build a self-contained example-topic landing page plus verify.py that proves it with headless Chrome rendering, section IDs, viewport meta, media query, no JS errors, and a PASS line. Let me first check the environment for available tooling (headless Chrome, Python packages) and the target directory.

Environment: google-chrome is installed, playwright browsers exist in ~/.cache/ms-playwright (chromium-1234) but the Python playwright/selenium modules are missing. I'll check for the `pyppeteer`/`websockets` options and the Chrome version, then decide how verify.py drives the browser.

Good: `google-chrome --headless=new --dump-dom` works (exit 0), and `websockets` 15.0.1 is available for console-error capture via CDP. Plan: verify.py drives headless Chrome via CLI + a small CDP listener for console errors. Now let me create the deliverable directory and write index

Directory created. Now I'll write the landing page. Content rules from the card: jargon-light, any number must be sourced in a visible footer link or left out. I'll write copy with only well-established qualitative facts (avoiding invented numbers), and put the sources in the footer.

Landing page written. Now the verify.py that proves all the done-when conditions: HTML parses, headless Chrome renders with hero headline + all section IDs, viewport meta + @media block present, no JS/console errors, and exits 0 printing one PASS line.
verify.py written. Let me run the proof command to test it — but I anticipate the `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete` pattern may be deprecated in Python 3.14. Let me run it and see.

The `/json/new` endpoint rejects GET (405) — newer Chrome requires PUT. Also I should simplify: I can attach to the browser-level websocket and use the built-in `Target.createTarget` instead of the HTTP endpoint. Let me patch `drive_page` to create the target via CDP on the browser websocket, which is the more robust modern approach.
Patched to use the flattened CDP session over the browser websocket (no HTTP `/json/new`). Let me run the proof again
The proof passes with exit 0 and one PASS line. Now let me run the official verdict tool to snapshot the proof output to the verdict log, as the card requires
Verdict PASS is recorded. Let me do a final self-check that the page truly makes no external requests (no external src/url()/import/fetch) before completing
All conditions verified: no external assets loaded (only 3 plain footer anchor links for sourcing, which the card requires), page is self-contained. Now completing the card.

Done — card t_d3c396cd complete. Shipped /home/user/projects/example-site/index.html (self-contained, plain HTML/CSS/JS, no external assets) + verify.py. Proof: `python3 .../verify.py` exits 0, one PASS line; headless Chrome renders all 6 section ids, hero headline, viewport meta + @media blocks, zero console/exception errors. Verdict tool: crew_card.py verdict --card t_d3c396cd → PASS (logged to verdicts/t_d3c396cd.jsonl). Note: copy uses no statistics (per card rule: numbers only if footer-sourced), so it is qualitative only; the 3 footer links are plain citation anchors, not loaded assets.
